message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Report Viewer Unit Test

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - ".github/workflows/report-viewer-test-unit.yml"
      - "report-viewer/**"

jobs:
  pre_job:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      should_skip: ${{ steps.skip_check.outputs.should_skip }}
    steps:
      - id: skip_check
        uses: fkirc/skip-duplicate-actions@v5
        with:
          concurrent_skipping: 'same_content_newer'
          skip_after_successful_duplicate: 'true'

  test:
    needs: pre_job
    if: ${{ needs.pre_job.outputs.should_skip != 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout 🛎️
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: report-viewer/package-lock.json

      - name: Install
        working-directory: report-viewer
        run: |
          npm install
      - name: Test model
        working-directory: report-viewer/model
        run: |
          npm run test
      - name: Test parser
        working-directory: report-viewer/parser
        run: |
          npm run test
      - name: Test ui-components
        working-directory: report-viewer/ui-components
        run: |
          npm run test
      - name: Test report-viewer
        working-directory: report-viewer/report-viewer
        run: |
          npm run test:unit",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs `npm install` on every pull-request run with no dependency cache, so dependencies are refetched each time. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (measured CI workflow on fork, ~6% elapsed savings) supports caching dependency downloads while keeping installation and all required tests intact. Adding `cache: npm` keyed on `report-viewer/package-lock.json` to the existing setup-node step reuses the npm package cache across runs, preserves every test step, adds no new network, privilege, secret, or deployment surface, and is a minimal change.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9"]
}
